blocks.text: Baseball is the people’s favorite sport in the United States. Little boys play baseball in parks and empty lots, in streets and alleys. Soccer, on the other hand, is preferred by most people in Europe and in most of Latin American countries.

Officially, the baseball season goes from April to September. At the end of the season when the two top teams play against each other to find the winner of the «World Series», excitement and tension rise in cities all over the country. Fans make long trips to watch the games and to shout from their seats in the bleachers.
Football, which begins its season in Autumn, attracts greater crowds at each game than baseball. There are many huge stadiums throughout the country, some seating 100,000 and more.

Basketball season follows football season. The game was invented in the United States, to provide an indoor game that could be played in the evening and during the winter. Its fast play and high scores make it a fascinating game to play and watch.

Just in recent years, winter sport have become extremely popular. Cities have ice rinks where skaters can keep in practice all year round when the ponds are no longer frozen. Ski resorts have become a thriving business, and ski lifts, once a real novelty, are springing up on slopes all over the northern part of the U.S., where snow can be expected.
Americans have certainly become more interested in sports in recent years and the increased sale of sporting equipment shows the rising interest.

items.q: How many months does the baseball season take?
Why are football stadiums bigger than baseball stadiums?
Why can people play basketball in the winter?
What makes it possible to skate in the summer?

blocks.text: Mr. George Bates takes his daughter Vicky to a baseball game.

items: *George:* Will you hurry up, Vicky? The game has already started.
*Vicky:* It’s not my fault if we’re late. It’s taken you a long time to park the car.
*George:* O.K. Let’s hurry. Our seats are over there.
*Vicky:* You know I can’t sit in the sun. It isn’t good for my complexion.
*George:* You won’t have to sit in the sun. Our seats are in the grandstand.
*Vicky:* Do you usually sit in the grandstand?
*George:* No, I’d rather sit in the bleachers. It’s cheaper. Hey, look at those two seats behind the home plate.
*Vicky:* Well, here we are. I hope you will tell me about the game.
*George:* Sure. Good heavens! They’ve already been playing for over twenty minutes. The Yankees scored two runs in the second inning.
*Vicky:* There are nine innings in a game, aren’t there?
*George:* That’s right. Except when the score is tied after completing the ninth inning. Then they play extra innings until the tie is broken.
*Vicky:* Who’s that man getting ready to throw the ball?
*George:* That’s the pitcher.
*Vicky:* And I suppose the player who will try to hit the ball is the batter – isn’t that right?
*George:* Oh, you seem to know much more about baseball than I imagined. Look … the pitcher has thrown the ball.
*Vicky:* And the batter has missed it. That man dressed in blue and wearing a mask has just shouted, «strike!»
*George:* That’s the umpire. He decides whether the pitcher has thrown a ball or a strike.
*Vicky:* He must be an important person.

*George:* Yes. Though some fans wouldn’t agree with you, especially when their decisions go against their favorite team’s interest. Well, that’s the last out. The Yankees beat the Red Socks two to nothing.

items.q: Did they get late to the game?
What’s the relation between Mr. Bates and the girl?
Where does George prefer to sit? Why?
What happens when the score is tied after finishing the ninth inning?
Why do some fans hate the umpire on some occasions?

Which sport would you like to take up?
